episode_thesis: Prince's career interview: Bridgewater's method is a coded, first-principles system integrating economy and markets, with hidden market exposures identified and hedged and long history used to test ideas. He sees modern mercantilism and geopolitical disruption as a lasting regime threatening the macro balance achieved after five years of instability.

speakers.name: Bob Prince
speakers.speaker_note: Auto-captions misspell Bridgewater and Ray Dalio ('Rey', 'Ry'). The interviewer asks questions and is not mapped. Interview is mostly career story; method content is thin and mostly principle-level.

worldview_premises.premise: Economies and markets are one integrated system; the edge is merging an economist's understanding of how the economy works with a trader's understanding of flows, risk and reward.
worldview_premises.support: Bridgewater's design as he saw it as a client.

worldview_premises.premise: Companies and people carry hidden market bets (a jeweler is long gold; Tulsa is long oil; Caterpillar is short a strong dollar), so profits blend operating skill and market exposure.
worldview_premises.support: Personal observation: Illinois layoffs when the dollar was strong, Tulsa 3% vs Boston 18% unemployment, then oil bust.

worldview_premises.premise: Derive answers from first principles ('basic physics of how the world works'), independent of others; convention settles in, and if you are right the world comes to you.
worldview_premises.support: Bridgewater's growth came from repeated cases of this.

worldview_premises.premise: A diversified portfolio can fall together in a deflationary depression; long-duration bonds give leveraged hedge exposure.
worldview_premises.support: Kodak's CIO question tested on data back to the 1860s.

worldview_premises.premise: Markets are zero-sum and returns are the objective standard of right or wrong; a firm lacking internal meritocracy will not compete.
Risk lies in what you do not know; humility and people with different capabilities show blind spots.
Economics textbooks rest on false assumptions and no book explains how the world works; one must ask own questions and find own answers.
Small differences in compounding rate become huge over long horizons, so play the long game.
worldview_premises.support: 10% vs 5% over 40 years gives roughly six times.

worldview_premises.premise: Globalisation produced imbalances that bred leaders favouring government involvement; modern mercantilism is a lasting philosophical change.

decision_process.practice: Code the view into rules and trade it, so outcomes are judged honestly rather than adjusting the story.
Group work: no single decision maker; research and plans are team efforts.
Check a forecaster's past published reports for accuracy before buying; assemble long history (1860s data) to test claims.
Global long/short in any market; first alpha-overlay mandate with 25-year target duration, 2-2.5x leverage, futures-based.
decision_process.why: Not a sitting duck; combine hedge and alpha.

decision_process.practice: Risk-management plans: identify and hedge latent market exposures.
Hiring ranks values, ability, then skills.

speakers.evidence_style: First principles, long historical data series, track-record checks of forecasters, and personal anecdote; no performance data or backtests shown.

current_views.view: Clash of stability and instability: policy makers restored balance across countries after five years of imbalances, but geopolitical chaos (tariffs, boycotts) threatens it.
current_views.reasoning: Imbalances from COVID, overheating and tight money were corrected; tariffs and boycotts threaten them.

current_views.view: Modern mercantilism (inward focus, competition, more government) will be with us for a while.
current_views.reasoning: A philosophical change, led by China, then Biden and Trump.

current_views.view: Europe is left behind in mercantilism but German defence spending is unintended fiscal stimulus.

gaps_and_conflicts.issue: Method statements are principle-level; no mechanism, signal or performance detail on the systems he describes.
He values being radically different from consensus yet says all of Bridgewater's decisions are group efforts avoiding single decision-makers; no conflict stated but tension.
The Kodak study is called the 'gold standard' but its first Monday attempt 'really sucks'; results and conclusions of the study are not given.
Economics textbooks said to rely on false assumptions without naming any.
The compounding example (10% vs 5%) is applied to learning rates, which is a metaphor not a measurable quantity.

forward_looking_inputs: (reader) Whether geopolitical disruptions (tariffs, boycotts) overturn the restored cross-country balance; European fiscal expansion (German defence); strong dollar effects on exporters; commodity price swings on commodity-dependent regions. No explicit horizon beyond 'for a while'.
reader_inferences: (reader) Prince's hedge-the-latent-exposure idea implies measuring a firm's return as operating margin plus embedded factor bets.
(reader) The 1991 mandate shows the origin of treating duration and currency as tradeable alpha dimensions.
